title: A gather the compiler can prove
starter:
%d   = buffer 4 [10 20 30 40] dtype=i32 slot=0
%ix  = buffer 1 [2] dtype=i32 slot=1
%res = buffer 1 dtype=i32 slot=2
# res[0] = d[i], where i comes from ix[0]. A negative i reads d[0];
# any other i reads d[i mod 4]. The view must be provably in bounds.
%i0  = shrink %ix 0 []
%i   = load %i0
%src = shrink %d %i []
%v   = load %src
%r0  = shrink %res 0 []
%s   = store %r0 %v
%r1  = after %res %s
hints: The starter is invalid: `%i` is loaded from memory, so its interval is all of i32, and the compiler can't prove `shrink %d %i` is inside `%d`.
Two ops shape the interval and the behavior: `max %i 0` sends every negative index to 0, then `mod` by 4 brings the result down to `[0, 3]`.
`mod %i 4` alone is already `[0, 3]` (mod floors, so it never goes negative), and the view would be valid. But a negative i must read d[0], and `-5 mod 4` is 3. Do the `max` first.
explain: `max %i 0` has bounds `[0, INT_MAX]`, and `mod` by a fixed 4 has bounds `[0, 3]`, so `shrink %d %k shape=[]` is provably inside 4 elements. The `max` isn't needed for the proof any more (floor `mod` by 4 is in `[0, 3]` on its own), but it gives the asked-for behavior: negative indices read d[0], and big ones wrap mod 4.
